headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 4 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Onto the Andorran rollercoaster! After stage 3 had to be cancelled due to extreme weather, the race resumes with a mountain stage entirely held in the Principality: a 104.8 km loop around Andorra La Vella packing 2,953 metres of elevation with relentless ups and downs over the Port d’Envalira, Collada de Beixalis, Coll d’Ordino and Alto de La Comella. The neutral start is set at 14:40, the start proper at 14:49 after a 2.5 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: The 3rd country of La Vuelta 26
subtext: After Monaco and France, it’s time for Andorran racing. As of tomorrow, La Vuelta will settle in Spain, the fourth country on this edition’s route. The race visited four countries last year too: Italy, France, Andorra, and Spain.

headline: Andorra la Vella, a classic of La Vuelta
subtext: Andorra la Vella is a classic of La Vuelta since the Spanish Grand Tour first ventured in Andorra, in 1965. On day 11, the race went from Barcelona to Andorra la Vella, passing Collada de Toses and Port d’Envalira. Spain’s Esteban Martin won the stage and Rolf Wolfshohl retained the overall lead, en route to success a week later in Bilbao. The last La Vuelta stage winner in Andorra la Vella is Vincenzo Nibali, on day 3 of the 2017 edition. Last year, Andorra la Vella hosted the start of stage 7 of La Vuelta. Juan Ayuso won the stage in Cerler and Torstein Træn retained La Roja after he took the overall lead the day before, already in Andorra (Pal).

headline: Good memories for Kuss and Skjelmose
subtext: In 2021, the Tour de France also had a stage finish in Andorra la Vella, after summiting Port d’Envalira and Collada de Beixalis. Sepp Kuss took what remains the last USA Tour stage win to date. Since 2025, Andorra la Vella is the start of the Andorra MoraBanc Classica. Like today’s stage, the course takes on the climbs of Port d’Envalira, Col d’Ordino and Alto de la Comella. The finish is then set at Coll de la Botella. Mattias Skjelmose won the first edition ahead of Cristian Rodriguez and Enric Mas. Also among the participants in La Vuelta 26, Sepp Kuss was 3rd this year.

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 2.5 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Stage 3 brought no change to the overall standings as it was cancelled. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) wears La Roja for a third consecutive day. He is followed by two Visma-Lease a Bike riders: Wout van Aert (+9’’) and yesterday’s stage winner, Matthew Brennan (+10’’). Today’s course is set to reshuffle the GC.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: With his victory in the ITT and his place of third in Manosque, Tadej Pogacar leads the points standings with 42 points. Since he races with La Roja, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) will be wearing the green jersey again. The British rouleur has 37 points. Matthew Brennan follows with the 30 points he took in Manosque.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla) dominated the first two categorised climbs of La Vuelta 26 to become the first leader of the KOM standings with 6 points. Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) took 4 points, while Ethan Hayter and Sinuhe Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) have 1 point each.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Matthew Brennan’s first Grand Tour stage win came with a distinctive jersey: the young British sprinter leads the young riders standings with gaps of 2 seconds to Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and 4’’ to Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe).

headline: Team standings
subtext: UAE Emirates XRG still lead the team standings with a gap of 3’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike and 23’’ to Netcompany Ineos.

headline: Heading for Encamp, forever associated with Pogacar's rise to glory
subtext: Early in the stage (km 1.7), the race passes by Encamp, a few kilometres below Els Cortals d’Encamp, where Tadej Pogacar took his first Grand Tour stage win in La Vuelta 19 (stage 9), a couple of weeks before his 21st birthday. Since then, he has won 36 Grand Tour stages: - 26 in the Tour - 6 in the Giro - 4 in La Vuelta (3 in 2019, 1 in 2026) Today, he returns to Encamp with La Roja on his shoulders. He has earned 94 Grand Tour overall leader jerseys (71 in the Tour, 20 in the Giro, 3 in La Vuelta). All in all, he has earned 241 distinctive jerseys in Grand Tours: - 94 as the overall leader - 6 as the leader of the points standings - 59 as the leader of the KOM standings - 82 as the leader of the young riders standings Els Cortals d’Encamp also saw Mikel Landa take his first (and so far only) La Vuelta stage win, in 2015. Read more about Tadej Pogacar’s spectacular Grand Tour debut at La Vuelta 19

headline: Stage 4 is ON!
subtext: Early attackers immediately set off.

headline: Uriarte attacks, UAE already control
subtext: Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) has opened a gap after 1 kilometre of racing. A Tadej Pogacar teammate (Ivo Oliveira?) sets the pace at the front of the peloton.

headline: Attacking towards the highest summit of La Vuelta 26
subtext: At 2,409 metres of altitude, Port d’Envalira is the highest summit of La Vuelta 26. The other 2,000+ summit of this edition is Calar Alto (2,153m), the finish of stage 12. Already passed during the first La Vuelta stage in Andorra (1965), Port d’Envalira has often featured in the Spanish Grand Tour, as well as the Tour de France and also the Volta a Catalunya. The last rider to go first at the summit is Sylvain Moniquet during the Andorra MoraBanc Classica, last June. Alejandro Valverde won the only La Vuelta stage that finished at Port d’Envalira, in 2003.

headline: A dozen riders on the move
subtext: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) and a dozen more attackers want to get away on the first slopes up Port d'Envalira.

headline: Kuss is among the early attackers
subtext: Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) spoke about his ambitions for today's stage: "Of course it would be nice to try to win the stage today, I'll give my best and try to enjoy the complete stage in Andorra. It will be tough, only the fourth stage. It will be a big stage. The race just goes by so much faster when you know every part of the road. Of course it feels different in a race than in training but hearing my name from people I know is really special. Today it's only up and down so it's pretty simple, just a matter of legs. It's a short stage and it doesn’t hurt to try something."

headline: Around 40 riders on the move
subtext: We can see Matthew Brennan, Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike), Ivan Romeo (Movistar), Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla), Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious)... UAE Emirates XRG drive the bunch a handful of seconds behind.

headline: Almeida bridges the gap to the breakaway
subtext: His teammates still pace the bunch a dozen seconds behind the leaders after 7 kilometres.

headline: Uijtdebroeks among the early stragglers
subtext: The Belgian climber is affected by his crash on day 1.

headline: The battle goes on
subtext: At km 9, eight riders try to get away after the peloton caught the large group on the move. Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) is up there.

headline: 14 leaders at km 11
subtext: The move initiated with Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) is consolidating. Matthew Brennan is up there again, along with Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike). Pablo Castrillo Movistar (Movistar) just bridged the gap.

headline: The leaders: Van Aert, Tulett, Fortunato, Fisher-Black...
subtext: Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Pablo Castrillo, Raul Garcia Pierna (Movistar), Wout van Aert, Bruno Armirail, Matthew Brennan, Ben Tulett (Visma-Lease a Bike), Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN), Simon Dalby (Uno X Mobility), Paul Double (Jayco AlUla), Georg Steinhauser (EF Education-EasyPost), Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana), Mattia Gaffuri (Picnic PostNL) are now 42'' ahead of the bunch after 14 kilometres. Ivan Sosa (Kern Pharma) and Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) are brdiging the gap. Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) drives the bunch. Joao Almeida has suffered a mechanical.

headline: Visma vs UAE
subtext: After 17 kilometres, the gap is up to 1 minute, with Visma-Lease a Bike driving the breakaway and UAE Emirates XRG pulling the bunch. Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) is dropped from the breakaway as his teammate Jan Hirt joins the front group. Sergio Samitier (Cofidis) and Mario Aparicio (Burgos Burpellet BH) are also bridging the gap. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) leads the virtual standings as he only trails by 9'' in GC. Matthew Brennan (10'') and Fisher-Black (14'') are also up there. Joao Almeida (UAE Emirates XRG) is back in the bunch after his mechanical.

headline: Decathlon CMA CGM pull the bunch
subtext: Felix Gall said this morning he wanted a hard stage to gain time in the overall standings.

headline: Gall: "Tadej will do his own thing"
subtext: Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) described his approach to today's stage at the start: “Tadej [Pogacar] will do his own thing, I believe. I think he will just be the strongest by far, and then I hope I can be in the mix to make the difference today in the GC with maybe a few other guys. I think it depends when the race is gonna blow up, if it already happens on the steep climb, the second climb of the day, I think it’s possible. I hope I will be there.”

headline: 5 kilometres to the summit of Port d'Envalira
subtext: The gap from the leaders to the peloton is down to 35''. Some of the early attackers have been dropped: Sergio Samitier, Wout van Aert, Finn Fisher-Black, Maurio Aparicio... Matthew Brennan is currently setting a strong pace.

headline: 10 riders at the front
subtext: Brennan sets the pacewith nine riders on his wheel: Double, Tulett, Fortunato, Castrillo, Garcia Pierna, Dunbar, Sosa, Dalby, Hirt. They are 3 kilometres away from the summit

headline: Armirail returns to the front group
subtext: The last gap to the bunch: 37 seconds.

headline: Brennan is spent
subtext: After he set a strong pace at the front, Matthew Brennan is dropped from the breakaway with 2 km to go to the summit. Bruno Armirail has also been distanced again. Meanwhile, Sander De Pestel (Decathlon CMA CGM) brings the gap down to 28''.

headline: Double accelerates inside the final kilometre of ascent
subtext: The break explodes. And so does the bunch.

headline: Fortunato coquers the Port d'Envalira
subtext: Double opened the sprint but the Italian climber passed him at the summit.

headline: Results at Port d’Envalira (cat. 1, km 25.1)
subtext: 1. Fortunato, 10 pts 2. Double, 6 pts 3. Sosa, 4 pts 4. Castrillo, 2 pts 5. Tulett, 1 pt

headline: Konrad: "I have really good memories"
subtext: In 2021, Patrick Konrad (Lidl-Trek) won a Tour de France stage starting from Pas de la Casa, also featured on today’s route (km 29.9): “I have really good memories. A victory at the Tour is something every cyclist dreams about and I’m also really proud of it. Today, I go very motivated into the stage. I love Andorra to prepare big races in altitude. I know today’s stage really well and with that memory of winning a Tour de France stage starting in Andorra I’m highly motivated. The job is clear for me for the whole Vuelta, to support ‘Skjelly’ [Mattias Skjelmose] and Mads [Pedersen] as good as possible in the next three weeks to reach our goals. The second climb will be really challenging, so I really hope to have good legs there to be in the final with Skjelly and support him as good as possible. Today is a really good stage already to make a difference for the GC. I will not be surprised if UAE put the hammer down today and go all in already on the second climb. On the first one, there will be a super high pace. I think they will destroy the peloton and it won’t be a comfortable or easy stage today, it will be really hard.”

headline: The attackers are caught on the downhill
subtext: Decathlon CMA CGM maintain a strong pace into the last 70 kilometres.
